description: Cosmic Mindshift is a beginner-friendly team passionate about Earth, space, data, and technology. We want to explore NASA Earth data, identify environmental trends, and create simple visual insights. We welcome curious teammates interested in Earth Science, Data Analysis, Data Visualization, Web Development, Design, AI/ML, and Storytelling. No expert needed, just teamwork, creativity, and willingness to learn!
summary: EarthLens BD is an interactive climate and environmental data explorer for Bangladesh, built with Python, Pandas, Plotly and Streamlit. It is designed around NASA POWER temperature and rainfall data and real NASA MODIS NDVI, and shows temperature and rainfall trends by division, temperature anomalies against a 2000–2010 baseline, NDVI green cover, monthly heatmaps, and flood/drought risk indices. Bangladesh is among the most climate-vulnerable countries, but NASA's Earth data is hard for students, planners and communities to read. EarthLens BD turns it into simple, filterable charts and downloadable CSVs, so anyone can see how the local climate is changing and which divisions face higher risk.
details:
EarthLens BD is an interactive web dashboard that makes climate and environment data for Bangladesh easy to explore. It shows temperature and rainfall trends by division, temperature anomalies against a 2000–2010 baseline, NDVI green cover charts, a monthly heatmap, a division map, flood and drought risk indices, a hottest-years ranking and a correlation heatmap. Users can filter the data and download it as a CSV file.

How it works: monthly 1 km NDVI from NASA MODIS (MOD13A3.061) is requested through NASA AppEEARS, and a script in our repository can download monthly temperature and rainfall from NASA POWER. Pandas cleans the data and calculates baselines, anomalies and risk indices. Plotly draws the charts and maps, and Streamlit turns everything into an interactive app that runs in a browser.

Data status: The demo uses real NASA MODIS NDVI (MOD13A3.061, monthly, Feb 2000 to Dec 2023), sampled at one point per division, so a single pixel may differ from the division as a whole. Temperature and rainfall are synthetic sample data by default; a script to download real NASA POWER temperature and rainfall is included in the repository.

Benefits: students, planners and communities can see how local climate and vegetation change without handling raw satellite data. It supports awareness of heat, flood and drought risk.

Intended impact: to help people and decision makers in Bangladesh understand environmental change, using NASA POWER and NASA MODIS data as the real data sources. The app is free, open source (MIT license) and needs no sign-in.

Tools: Python, Pandas, Plotly, Streamlit, pytest, GitHub and GitHub Actions.

Creativity: a Bangladesh-focused "trend detective" view with division-level comparison, risk indices and one-click data export, in a simple layout for non-experts.

Factors considered: data accuracy, simplicity for non-technical users, open access, and being transparent in our documentation about what is real data and what is sample data.

Next steps: real NASA POWER temperature and rainfall as the default data, division-wide NDVI averages, and district-level analysis with GeoPandas.
